data.name: Warp Frontier
data.detailed_description:
Vincent Cassini, decorated war hero, but still just a Captain in the police force he started, is patrolling the orbital slums of his home planet Cetus, when he stumbles across a lead in a war crime that resulted in the mysterious disappearance of thousands of Cetans, including his first wife and best friend. Captain Cassini and his robot partner MAC, must ally with morally questionable characters to stop an old enemy before their crimes are erased forever.



Solve puzzles in point and click adventure style and navigate Vince’s relationships with his family, allies and enemies. The decisions you make and the order in which you undertake tasks result in varying outcomes each playthrough, potentially costing the lives of thousands. Your actions ultimately decide what type of father, partner, friend, officer and saviour Vince will be.



  • Make decisions that affect the lives of thousands of people, and determine relationships between family and friends
  • A 2D point and click adventure in HD
  • 6-8 hours of gameplay with branching decisions, resulting in multiple unique ending sequences
  • Authentic Australian feel, voiced by a predominantly Australian cast
  • An alternate timeline of humanity branching from a catastrophic singularity event
  • Original Soundtrack by Thomas Regin
  • Explore space in your own ship, from the planet surface to the outer reaches of the planetary ring

reviews.review:
[h1][b][u]BottomLine at the Top:[/u][/b][/h1] Excellent.  Only major gripe is that extensive use of multiple choices would have been better served by additional save slots. 

[h1][b][u]Intro:[/u][/b][/h1] 

As always full disclosure first, I was given a review copy of this game for free from the developer (greatly appreciated as always!).  It was a pleasant surprise as I had my eye on this title for awhile and would most likely have picked it up regardless.  Overall, a great sci-fi P&C experience... but could have been damn near perfect with a few modifications.  

-------------------------------------
[h1][b][u]Pros:[/u][/b][/h1]
-------------------------------------
-Starts right up, no set up nonsense.  Stable, never crashed during gameplay.
-Engrossing story with interesting worldbuilding and good writing.  I take notes when writing reviews and I've come to find the more time I go without writing anything down, positive or negative, the more interested I am in the game itself.
-Good quality of life features like a hotspot highlight function, basic autosave, double click fast walk, inventory scrolling via mouse wheel, and fantastic built in hint system (more on that later).
-Actually, scratch that, I'll talk about the hint system right now!  It’s a Universal Hint System (remember those guys?!?) with tiered clues that get more detailed the further along you go.  What I found interesting though is how well it adapted to where you were with a particular challenge.  In many cases (not all) if you were let’s say halfway through, the hint system would update with the info you already had.  This must have been an awful lot of extra work, but I noticed it early on as a running theme with this title, which namely is attention to detail.
-Speaking of detailed, the art is fantastic in this game.  Backgrounds, characters, inventory objects are all very well done.
-Another thing that this game has that I absolutely love to see is seeing detailed interactions between almost all inventory objects.  What I mean by this is the developers actually took the time to write responses many possible interactions.  It’s almost cliche to see a game call upon a few classic responses, you know the ones..."I can't do that", "I' don't want to do that", "that doesn't make any sense", etc...   When you get to that point in a P&C, again you know the ones (the "what the hell am I supposed to do point") and your greeted by these premade lazy responses, well its damn frustrating.  Your trying to throw everything at the wall and see what sticks. You end up playing "Who has the crazier moon logic" with the developer.  According to them it’s so clear that you need to stick the gum on the pineapple why can't you just see it... meanwhile you’re trying to match their craziness with your own and you just can’t see why the solution doesn't involve combining the bucket and the kazoo cause you justwantthedaMngAmetOmOvEFoRWaRdWHATTHEFU.... (:breathes:)......BUT I digress.  It’s so nice to see a game that takes the time to acknowledge that maybe you have a good idea there but it’s not what their looking for and doing so by utilizing a custom response prompt.  Or maybe your idea was stupid, but the game gives a funny comment.  Doing this takes a great deal more time than the generic response method, but it’s so worth it in terms of immersion that I wish more games took the time to do this.  
-Overall game flow is well balanced.  Puzzles are mostly in the sweet spot of challenging, but not frustrating. The few times I did get stuck the hint system was calibrated to the exact amount of clues I needed.
-Takes inspiration from ideas about the Technological Singularity.  As a card-carrying futurist, I approve!
-Well voice acted.  Professional production.
-Music and sound effects good.

-------------------------------------
[h1][b][u]Meh...:[/u][/b][/h1]
-------------------------------------
-So, the info bar at the top is an interesting mechanic.  It essentially acts as combination of an auto "look" icon, a way to keep track of what objective you should be focused on, and an inner monologue of the main character.  I guess by the end of the game I got used to it, but the classic P&C lover in me might have liked a "look" icon.  
-This is a minor aesthetic gripe; it'd be nice if the menu/hint buttons in the corner would minimize or hide themselves unless you brought the cursor over that area or something.  
-Inventory does not auto reorganize when items are used/removed.
-Dialogue interface is standard in that new/unanswered questions appear in white and grey out if they have been asked.  That’s a good thing.  However, the control of the ship is through a dialogue interface.  This leads to previously selected commands turning grey, even if they need to be used multiple times in the game.  Sometimes it updates, usually with navigation, but not always.
-This was a pre-release version so there are a few minor programming bugs/inconveniences that I'm sure will be worked out eventually.  (Things like MAC continuing to hold open doors on screens that have reused backgrounds but are actually different locations, one case of a new sprite taking up so much space I had to find a sweet spot to move to the other side of the screen, the previously described ship controls, and probably a couple other things I didn't bother to remember but didn't really subtract from the overall experience).
-Wasn't super plused having a confirmation tone play after every dialog choice made at the beginning of the game.  I'm not sure if I just got used to it or it eventually stopped.
-MAC as a sidekick.  Full Stop.  He's with you the whole game and for most of it he's just Meh... Which is really unfortunate as its a ROBOT SIDEKICK.  He's got a few good lines I guess but...idk...meh.

-------------------------------------
[h1][b][u]Cons:[/u][/b][/h1]
-------------------------------------
-Without giving too much away... the ending felt abrupt and was somewhat confusing.  Though it does leave open room for a sequel, I kind of was expecting another 30-60 minutes of game play before I reached the end.  
-I put that first con at the top to give perspective to my biggest caveat with the game which I'll list here: there are only 4 save slots.  If you've read any of my other P&C reviews, you'll know this is a pet-peeve of mine.  Usually, the degree of dislike I have for this ranges from "meh, doesn’t really matter but still..." to "fundamentally alters the quality of the gaming experience". Unfortunately given this game’s large use of branching choices, lack of save slots puts this more into the red zone for this issue.  I'm not a huge Steam achievements guy, but I do like checking out the various endings in a branching game like this.  I completed the game in about 6 hours and had only unlocked 36 of 69 (nice) achievements.  My ending was close to ideal but there was one or two things I would have liked to have experimented with.  But, I was lazy in utilizing my save slots so all 4 were used within the last hour of the game.  I couldn’t go back to try some other variables without basically restarting the game.  And although I really did enjoy this title, I'm not a big replay guy these days (my backlog of unplayed games is just too big and my free time too little).  Had I the extra save slots, I probably would have jumped around to try different options but I'm not about to go start a whole new game to check these things out.  


[h1][b][u]Final Thoughts:[/u][/b][/h1] 

This game kept reminding me of a few of my fav Sci-Fi P&C games.  Titles like Beneath a Steel Sky, Neofeud, Mission Critical, Blade Runner, Technobabylon, and Whispers of a Machine all come to mind.  Being in that kind of echelon of adventure... well honestly, I can't think of a higher honor to bestow on a good Sci-Fi P&C game!  Highly recommended for the P&C afficionado or any Sci-Fi fan!

[hr][/hr]
